title: Types of rights
log: 2026-10-29T12:14:26Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Types of rights
card: rights that protect a person's freedom and let them take part in public life. Examples are free speech, a fair trial and the right to vote.
rights that relate to a person's basic needs and way of life. Examples are education, health care, fair work and taking part in cultural life.
rights held by a group or a people, not by one person alone. An example is the right of a people to self-determination, which is choosing their own political status and future.
One law or case can involve more than one type. Sorting a right means asking who holds it and what it protects.
draft.remember: Ask who holds the right and what it protects: freedoms and public voice, basic needs and way of life, or a group's shared claim.

a.q: Which of these is an example of a civil and political right?
opts: The right to vote in an election
The right to attend a local school
The right to health care when sick
The right of a people to choose their future
a.why: Voting lets a person take part in public life, so it is a civil and political right. Education is tempting because it is a major right, but it relates to a basic need, so it is economic, social and cultural.
a.clue: Which right is about taking part in public life?

b.q: A group of Pacific islanders says that their people have the right to decide their own political status. What type of right are they claiming?
b.why: The claim is made by a people as a group, and it concerns self-determination, so it is a collective right. It is tempting to call it civil and political because it involves politics, but that type protects individuals, such as their vote or speech.
b.clue: Who holds this right: one person or a whole people?

a.best: The right to vote in an election
